podcasts.title: Scott Kupor on Building a16z and Rebuilding the Federal Workforce
podcasts.summary: Scott Kupor helped build a16z from three people into a firm with hundreds of employees. Now, as Director of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management, he’s applying some of the same lessons about talent, incentives, and organizational design to a workforce of roughly two million federal employees. Scott joins Founders host David Senra to tell the story of a16z’s earliest days, from joining Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz during the 2008 financial crisis to borrowing Michael Ovitz’s CAA model to build a venture firm around specialized networks and services for founders. He explains why a16z chose to market itself when venture firms traditionally didn’t, how early wins like Skype accelerated the firm’s growth, and why it eventually reorganized around specialized investing teams. Then they turn to Scott’s move into government. He lays out his effort to build a more merit-based federal workforce, attract younger technical talent, and create what he calls “permissioned risk” so government employees can actually try new things. That includes everything from changing how performance and promotions work to replacing a retirement process that still relied on hundreds of millions of pieces of paper stored in an underground Pennsylvania mine. podcasts.title: The Health Interventions Actually Worth Your Time | Justin Mares
podcasts.summary: Health advice has become an endless stream of supplements, diets, wearables, and biohacks. Which interventions are actually worth your time? Truemed CEO Justin Mares argues that most people should ignore the extremes and focus on a few fundamentals: better food, movement, sleep, and reducing harmful exposures. Justin joins a16z General Partner Daisy Wolf to walk through his own approach to health, from what he eats and how he exercises to supplements, blood tests, sauna, sleep, and the changes he’s made to his home. They also discuss the larger problem behind Truemed: while chronic disease drives the vast majority of U.S. healthcare spending, relatively little goes toward prevention. Justin explains how Truemed is trying to change that by making it easier for eligible consumers to use tax-free HSA and FSA dollars on qualified lifestyle interventions. podcasts.title: The New CFO: How AI Is Rewriting the Finance Function | Figma CFO Praveer Melwani
podcasts.summary: AI is moving finance from reconciling what happened last month to helping decide what the business should do next. Figma CFO Praveer Melwani argues that the best finance teams are becoming builders themselves, automating repetitive work so they can spend more time understanding customers, running experiments, and shaping strategy. Praveer joins a16z’s Seema Amble and Ivan Makarov to share what that shift looks like inside Figma, from collections and expense analysis to M&A diligence, where the corp dev team now uses AI to prototype products and simulate how Figma leaders might challenge an investment memo. They discuss why AI “slop” is a real risk, how Figma decides what to build versus buy, and why successful internal experiments eventually need a centralized systems layer to turn one-off agents into reliable infrastructure. They also get into what this means for hiring the next generation of finance leaders. Praveer’s bar isn’t simply whether someone can use AI. It’s whether they can understand the business, interrogate the output, communicate clearly, and use automation without outsourcing their thinking. podcasts.title: Tokenization, Agentic Trading, Harmonic: Robinhood's Mission to Expand Ownership with CEO Vlad Tenev
podcasts.summary: What does it mean to build wealth as an individual investor in today’s society, especially as gains continue to get concentrated into smaller groups of VCs or institutional investors? Robinhood’s CEO and co-founder Vlad Tenev has a vision that can be summed up in one word: Ownership. In this episode, Sarah Guo chats with Vlad to get a closer look at how Robinhood has evolved from a simple app to buy stocks at zero commission into a global conglomerate that allows customers to own across a wide variety of surfaces and asset classes. Vlad explains how Robinhood is helping users extend ownership amidst the current economy and ongoing AI revolution through Trump accounts, tokenization of privates, and newer product offerings like Robinhood Chain, Agentic Trading, and Agentic Credit Card. He also talks about how his new mathematical superintelligence startup, Harmonic, is revolutionizing the field and how he hopes it will decentralize new discoveries and inventions. Vlad and Sarah also discuss how prediction markets could tie into the ownership conversation, whether financial infrastructure can be optimized to enable even higher volumes of high-frequency trading, and his advice for maintaining a level head when facing the vagaries of a changing financial market.
